text: Hello and welcome to our live commentary of West Ham against Burnley!
With a place in next season's Europa League within reach, West Ham will be looking to add three more points and pile on the pressure on the teams above them.

The Hammers trail fifth-placed Tottenham Hotspur by eight points for a spot in the Europa League.Burnley, meanwhile, slumped 2-0 against Bournemouth at Turf Moor in their last league match, extending their winless streak to nine, leaving them in 19th place on 13 points, 11 points from safety with 11 matches to play.
Let’s take a look at the lineups for the clash at the London Stadium...
David Moyes makes four changes to his side after the Europa League defeat to Freiburg last Thursday night.
Whilst Areola resumes his Premier League goalkeeping duties, the more notable changes in the Hammers’ backline are the replacements of Emerson with Cresswell and Zouma giving way to Aguerd.
Phillips also starts ahead of Alvarez, and the former Manchester City midfielder will be keen to make an impression today and claim a more regular starting role.
Burnley, on the other hand, stick with the same starting 11 as the one that succumbed to a home defeat to Bournemouth last time around.
Vincent Kompany is clearly showing loyalty and trust in his regular starters – let’s see whether they can reward him, and the fans, with a more clinical performance.
The players are coming out and are ready for kick-off.
Here we go!
Burnley get us underway in their yellow away kit...
Burnley are edging forward into the West Ham defensive third but the Hammers’ defence deals with a Bruun Larsen comfortably and clears the ball away.
Trafford has it in his own box and looks to play out from the back.
Taylor this time delivers a loopy ball into the West Ham box but the resulting header is caught easily by Areola.
Fofana seems to have hurt himself in the kerfuffle in the box but the Burnley striker gets up quickly.
Now West Ham’s turn to threaten! Bowen plays a low cross into the Burnley area which eventually hits Kudus.
The forward then delivers a ball towards the back post which Assignon messily clears.
West Ham appealed for a handball off the Burnley defender but the flag was up for offside.
Pretty lively start from both sides here, with plenty to play for.
West Ham are still pushing for the European spots, while Kompany will not let his players lose sight of pushing out of the relegation zone.
Trafford plays a neat pass through the West Ham press and Burnley try to push forward.
The home side intercepts a loose ball but Coufal hits it straight out of play.
The ball is back again with the Burnley keeper, who has had plenty of touches already.

WHAT A GOOOALLLL!! 1-0 Burnley and it's Fofana with an unbelievable strike straight in the top bins, pick that one out! The Burnley striker works hard to win the ball from two West Ham midfielders, who won’t want to see that one again.
Fofana then hits one from well out the box, a solid 25 yards or so from goal, and it flies straight past Areola, who stood no chance as the effort sails into the top-right corner.
What a start for Burnley!
Burnley have started this game just how they started against Bournemouth last week – with confidence and clear possession.
The only difference, this time they’re on the scoresheet!
West Ham work the play well down the right side, and Coufal clips one into a dangerous area of the penalty box.
O’Shea connects to it first though, and the home side are trying to camp into the Burnley half now.
Assignon dribbles the ball through what appears to be quite legged West Ham midfielders.
He eventually loses out but you have to say, Burnley look the more sharper already with only 20 minutes on the clock.
The Europa League hangover might still be hitting the home players here.
Gareth Southgate looks on from the stands and you’ve got to wonder who from the West Ham team would challenge for a spot in the Euros squad at the moment, particularly from this opening phase!
Soucek blatantly pushes Cullen into Paqueta and Trafford lines up a free-kick from the halfway line.
The ball bounces off O'Shea and goes out for a goal-kick.
David Moyes won’t be happy with the start to the game from his players.
Burnley are the much more comfortable team on the ball, playing neat passes around the corner of West Ham midfielders, and the Hammers are second to best to a lot of the play here.
And right on queue, Mavropanos hits a pass straight out of play.
He’s not the only West Ham player to have done that either, we're not even 30 minutes in!
Kudus puts an early cross into the box but Bowen gets under it and heads it well away from the Burnley goal.
Paqueta tries to take matters into his own hands and drives with the ball straight through the middle of the Burnley midfield.
He eventually runs into too many men and has the ball nicked from his feet.
Mavropanos does really well to take the ball from Odobert and bulldoze his way through into the Burnley box.
He hits a left-footed attempt into the side netting but this is a lot better from West Ham.
They’re trying to get on the front foot now.
Soucek switches the ball over to Coufal, who is clumsily pushed over by Bruun Larsen.
The Hammers take the free-kick quickly but play a loose pass straight to Berge.
Burnley are now attempting to regain a bit of a hold on possession.
Bruun Larsen collects a long ball at the edge of the West Ham box but he’s deemed to be offside by a very late flag.
Bruun Larsen is involved again down the left as he does well to skip past Mavropanos.
Coufal is there to cover for his centre back though and Burnley have a corner.
Cullen is over the ball.
The resulting corner comes to nothing and Cullen collects the ball again towards the halfway line.
Kudus rushes to try and win the ball and knocks the Burnley midfielder over for a clear foul.
Taylor heads one back to Trafford who just about avoids it from going out for a corner.
Kompany applauds his players from the sideline and you can see why.
Burnley have controlled the majority of the game and limited West Ham to only a couple of half chances, and that’s being generous.
David Moyes won’t be happy going into half-time.
First yellow card of the game goes to Soucek for dragging Odobert.
A clear pull of the shirt and a deserved booking for the West Ham midfielder.
Bruun Larsen hits the resulting free-kick straight into Areola's arms.
A speculative effort really, considering how far out he was!
GOOALLL!! 2-0 Burnley and Mavropanos, look away now! Bruun Larsen plays a short pass into Cullen, who inside the box puts a low ball across the face of the West Ham goal.
Mavropanos is caught on his heels and makes an absolute mess of clearing the ball, instead putting it in his own goal.
You have to say, it’s nothing more than Burnley deserve for their continuous pressure.
What a way to end the half!
We’ve got three minutes of added time in this first half at the London Stadium.
Moyes will be eager to get into the dressing room and demand more from his players.
Kompany, however, will be more than pleased.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM 0-2 BURNLEY
Half-time here at a wet and rainy London Stadium, and one manager will be a whole lot more pleased than his counterpart going into the dressing room with Burnley winning 2-0.
Starting with the home side, West Ham have looked incredibly leggy off the ball, and even more sloppy on it.
Numerous astray passes, no threat on Trafford’s goal, and weak defending sums up their first-half performance.
And with only 0.08 xG, Moyes might look to his bench for some attacking inspiration.
Meanwhile, Burnley will want more of the same.
Fofana got the first goal of the game with a clean strike from 25 yards out – a Goal of the Month contender for sure.
Mavropanos then helped the away side and handed them the second goal on a plate, putting a fluffed clearance into his own net.
Burnley’s xG of 0.10 might suggest they haven’t been pressing West Ham’s defence, but far from it.
They have controlled the game and their patience has paid off so far.
Burnley are unbeaten in their last 11 Premier League matches when leading at half-time (W5, D6) dating back to August 2021.
West Ham on the other hand have a record of W1, D1, L5 when trailing at half-time this season.
It would take an early goal in the second half to try and turn this one around, you’d imagine, and the Hammers certainly need to pose more of an attacking threat if they want to trouble Burnley.
Kompany rolls the dice first with a substitution, replacing Bruun Larsen with Brownhill.
Moyes does not wait long to make a couple of West Ham subs.
Phillips' start for West Ham doesn't last long, and he's taken off for Alvarez.
The second West Ham substitute sees Ward-Prowse being replaced with Antonio, and Moyes is clearly looking to make the most of the momentum his side has gained.
We're underway for the second half!
GOAAALLL!! 2-1 and West Ham are back in it very quickly in the second half! Some really sloppy Burnley defending and Kompany will not be happy with his side’s defending.
A simple mix-up at the back for the Clarets and Paqueta capitalises.
The Brazilian knicks the ball from O’Shea close to the away side's box and slots it easily past Trafford.
Game on!
Ever since the first goal, West Ham have been pushing for a second.
They have had quick corners in succession and they’re causing a lot of issues for the Burnley defenders.
Moyes will be pleased with his team’s response in this half.
Good chance for Burnley to regain their two-goal lead.
They break quickly on a counter-attack led by Fofana, who dummies a shot to give himself some extra space but then hits his effort straight at Areola.
Just wide! Good play from substitute Antonio to cross the ball to Paqueta towards the opposite, right side of the Burnley box.
The midfielder sets his aims for the top left corner and only narrows hits his shot wide.
Vitinho hits a deflected shot just wide of Areola and wins Burnley a corner, but also some breathing space after some relentless West Ham pressure so far this half.
Paqueta has really come to life this half.
He collects a loose ball and curls one towards the bottom corner.
Trafford can collect easily though.
Esteve looks hurt here and is getting some treatment.
After some time, he’s now waiting for the referee to allow him back on the pitch.
First yellow card for Burnley goes to Assignon for time-wasting, and the defender will be on a tightrope for the remainder of the game.
Big chance for Kudus! The Ghanaian attacker takes it down well in the Burnley box and then cleverly skips past Vitinho onto his right foot.
Well inside the box, he has all of the goal to aim for but absolutely skies it.
A massive opportunity missed there.
Kompany is looking to sure things up at the back here, swapping the attacker Odobert for defender Delcroix.
A lot of heavy challenges flying in here from both sides.
If it wasn’t competitive already, it certainly is now with 20 minutes spare.
Antonio has done really well to win loose balls for his side since coming on.
Yet again the attacker bullies Delcroix off the ball to win the home team a throw-in close to Burnley’s box.
Delcroix gets himself in the book for time-wasting, which is emphasising Burnley's desperation to see this one over the line.
That's two of their defenders in the book for the same reason.
Superb work again from Antonio to win West Ham a corner.
He’s really up for a fight today and his teammates wouldn’t go wrong by being more direct, as the Burnley defenders are struggling to deal with physically.
Another one of his crosses finds its way to Coufal, whose ball into the box is deflected onto Trafford's bar!
Berge with a wrestling takedown on Bowen there.
One of the easiest yellow cards the referee will give out.
West Ham are really tallying up their corner count, and with Burnley’s deficiencies from dealing with set-pieces, they might fancy their chances from scoring from one.
Time is ticking for West Ham to get an equaliser, and Moyes clearly recognises that too.
Ings is coming on for Aguerd.
That's a reckless one from Paqueta who clashes with Burnley defender Esteve and gets himself a yellow.
Esteve is the third Burnley defender on a yellow now, and the centre back deservedly finds himself in the referee's book for a reckless challenge on Paqueta.
GOAALLL! Danny Ings makes an instant impact and equalises against his former side, but there's a VAR check for an offside...
DISALLOWED! West Ham thought they'd turned this game on its head but Antonio was deemed to be in an offside position in the build-up to Ings touching it past Trafford.
Burnley will be super relieved and are still holding on for the win here...
It remains 2-1.
Eight minutes added on here.
Will it be enough for the home side to get an equaliser?
GOOOALLL! And this one will stand, 2-2 West Ham! Ings was denied the earlier effort for an offside, but there’s no questioning this goal.
A cross into the box is deflected into his path, and the striker does incredibly to control and turn inside the box and volley past Trafford.

events.action: turn inside the box and volley past Trafford

text: For Burnley, they should know more than most that you can’t give a player of Ings’ quality so much space to turn and shoot.
Some second half from West Ham here.
Kompany takes off Vitinho for the more natural attacker, Gudmundsson.
How have West Ham not scored a third?!? A number of dangerous crosses into the penalty area, and the latest one falls perfectly for Ings at the edge of the box.
Again, the striker hits a volley towards his former side’s goal and hits the bar! What an effort
A game of two halves here, and West Ham will be kicking themselves for some of their missed chances if they don’t find a winner.
Huge appeals for a handball from West Ham are turned down.
You have to say, it looks like Berge headed the ball blatantly onto his arms.
West Ham will feel hard done by for sure.
Burnley almost steal it at the end! A counter-attack down the right side led by Gudmundsson is played to Berge, who then lays a clever ball to Brownhill.
The Burnley midfielder has a great chance to put it past Areola for the winner, but hits it straight at the keeper.
In fairness, four West Ham defenders were stood on the line ready to block the ball, but a big opportunity nonetheless.
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM 2-2 BURNLEY
Wow, what an end to a contest, which somehow finishes 2-2! West Ham will be wondering how they couldn’t find a winner, while Burnley will be disappointed to let their winning position slip.

The Clarets went into half-time with a comfortable 2-0 lead, and looked the sharper of the two sides after Fofana smashed a ferocious opener before Mavrapanos’ own goal gave the hosts a mountain to climb.
The second half was a whole different matter though, as Paqueta halved the deficit with not even a minute played.
Former Burnley man Ings then saw an equaliser ruled out by the VAR for offside but it didn’t take long for him to respond with a clever turn and volley to level.
Both sides had late chances to get the winner, and you feel a point does neither side any favours.
The home team ended with an xG of 1.93 and edged possession with 52 per cent, turning their attention again to the Europa League next week.
Burnley’s xG of 0.65 couldn’t trouble the Hammers in the second half and the Clarets will want to replicate the first-half performance against Brentford in the league.
